topic: How provenance, attestation and integrity standards record and verify evidence, as a benchmark for Fetchproof's hash-chained ledger
notes: Owner pages per unknown, no queries: every owner URL is known (W3C TR for PROV-DM, the in-toto attestation repository for the Statement, the DSSE envelope and the spec README, docs.sigstore.dev for Rekor, rfc-editor.org for RFCs 3161, 6962 and 8785, slsa.dev for the provenance predicate). Budget: 14 scrapes and 3 searches on the metered transport; phase 0 (decompose, 2026-10-04) spent 3 searches and 3 scrapes on secondary context, so this plan holds 10 pages and leaves one scrape spare. Depth deep so maxScrapes is the cap. No --fallback. Run 1 (2026-10-04): 9 collected, 1 failed - https://docs.sigstore.dev/logging/sign-verify/ answered HTTP 404 and was dropped from the plan; the Rekor overview names the inclusion proof and the append-only property but not the signed entry timestamp. Run 2: Rekor's openapi.yaml, the spare scrape. 13 of 14 scrapes and 3 of 3 searches spent in all (3 scrapes and 3 searches by phase 0).

urls.why: U-1: W3C PROV-DM, the provenance data model - Entity, Activity, Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, generation time
U-2: the in-toto Statement - _type, subject digests, predicateType, predicate
U-2: the in-toto Envelope - the DSSE signing envelope, payloadType and signatures
U-2: the attestation framework overview - the layers (Envelope, Statement, Predicate, Bundle) and what each binds
U-3: Rekor overview - the transparency log, the signed entry timestamp and the inclusion proof
U-4: RFC 3161 Time-Stamp Protocol - what a time-stamp token proves about when a datum's hash existed
U-5: RFC 6962 Certificate Transparency - the Merkle tree hash, the audit path and the consistency proof
U-6: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme - number serialization, string escaping, property sorting, Unicode
U-7: SLSA provenance predicate v1.0 - buildDefinition, runDetails, builder, resolvedDependencies

U-3: Rekor's OpenAPI definition - the owner of inclusionProof (logIndex, rootHash, treeSize, hashes, checkpoint) and signedEntryTimestamp (signature over logID, logIndex, body and integratedTime); collected in a second run because /logging/sign-verify/ answered HTTP 404
